questions.stem: The functional group present in alkanoic acids is
questions.explanation: The carboxyl group -COOH combines a carbonyl and a hydroxyl on the same carbon, and its hydrogen is the one released as H+, which is what makes the compound acidic. Ethanoic acid, CH3COOH, is the familiar example.

distractorRationale.a: -OH alone is the hydroxyl group found in alkanols, which are not acidic in water
distractorRationale.b: -CHO is the aldehyde group found in alkanals
distractorRationale.d: -COO- is the ester linkage formed when an acid reacts with an alcohol

questions.stem: In the fermentation of glucose by yeast, the products are
questions.explanation: The enzyme zymase in yeast breaks glucose down anaerobically according to C6H12O6 -> 2C2H5OH + 2CO2. The carbon dioxide is what makes fermenting palm wine bubble and what raises bread dough.

distractorRationale.a: Fermentation is anaerobic and consumes rather than releases oxygen-containing gas of that kind
distractorRationale.c: Ethanoic acid forms only later, when bacteria oxidise the ethanol in the presence of air
distractorRationale.d: Methanol is toxic and is not a product of yeast fermentation

questions.stem: Ethanol is warmed with ethanoic acid in the presence of a few drops of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid. The sweet-smelling organic product is
questions.explanation: An alkanol and an alkanoic acid undergo esterification: CH3COOH + C2H5OH gives CH3COOC2H5 plus water. The concentrated acid acts as a catalyst and also removes water, pushing the reversible reaction towards the ester. Esters have characteristic fruity smells.

distractorRationale.b: Ethanal comes from partial oxidation of ethanol, which needs an oxidising agent rather than an acid
distractorRationale.c: A salt of this kind would require a base such as sodium hydroxide, not an alcohol
distractorRationale.d: Ethene is formed when ethanol is dehydrated at 170 degrees Celsius with no acid present

questions.stem: Two colourless liquids are provided, one ethanol and one ethanoic acid. Which test distinguishes them?

options.text: Add sodium metal; only one gives hydrogen
Add sodium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) solution; only one effervesces
Smell them; only one has an odour

questions.explanation: Only an acid liberates carbon dioxide from a hydrogencarbonate, so the ethanoic acid fizzes and the gas turns lime water milky, while ethanol shows no change. Sodium metal is no help because both liquids contain an -OH hydrogen and both release hydrogen with it.

distractorRationale.a: Both compounds react with sodium to give hydrogen, so this test cannot separate them
distractorRationale.c: Both have strong distinctive smells, and smelling laboratory reagents is unsafe practice
distractorRationale.d: Ethanol and ethanoic acid are both completely miscible with water

questions.stem: When ethanol is warmed with acidified potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI), the solution changes from

options.text: green to orange as ethanol is reduced
orange to green as ethanol is oxidised
purple to colourless as ethanol is oxidised
colourless to pink as ethanol is reduced

questions.explanation: The dichromate(VI) ion is orange and contains chromium in the +6 state. As it oxidises ethanol first to ethanal and then to ethanoic acid, it is itself reduced to the green Cr3+ ion, so the mixture turns from orange to green.

distractorRationale.a: The direction is reversed; ethanol is the substance being oxidised, not reduced
distractorRationale.c: Purple to colourless is the change shown by manganate(VII), a different oxidising agent
distractorRationale.d: Colourless to pink describes a phenolphthalein indicator change, unrelated to this reaction

questions.stem: Ethanol boils at 78 degrees Celsius while ethane, of similar molecular mass, boils at -89 degrees Celsius. The difference is due to

options.text: the higher molecular mass of ethanol

questions.explanation: The hydroxyl group puts a hydrogen atom directly onto a highly electronegative oxygen, so ethanol molecules attract one another through hydrogen bonds. These are far stronger than the van der Waals forces that are all ethane has, so much more energy is needed to separate ethanol molecules.

distractorRationale.a: Covalent bonds within molecules are not broken during boiling
distractorRationale.c: The molecular masses are 46 and 30, a difference far too small to explain a gap of 167 degrees
distractorRationale.d: Ethanol is a covalent molecular compound and contains no ions

questions.explanation: The functional group of alcohols is the hydroxyl group (-OH). This group is responsible for the characteristic properties of alcohols, including their solubility in water and their ability to form hydrogen bonds.

distractorRationale.a: The carboxyl group is characteristic of carboxylic acids, not alcohols.
distractorRationale.c: The carbonyl group is found in aldehydes and ketones, not in alcohols.
distractorRationale.d: The amino group is characteristic of amines, not alcohols.
